newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ROYALS FIRE MANAGER BOONE, HIRE CUBS HIT COACH MUSER.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ROYALS FIRE MANAGER BOONE, HIRE CUBS HIT COACH MUSER.

text.p: The Kansas City Royals fired manager Bob Boone on Wednesday and replaced him with Chicago Cubs batting coach Tony Muser.
Tony Muser, a member of the Cubs coaching staff for the past five years, signed a contract with the Royals that lasts through the end of next season, the American League team said.
Kansas City is currently in fourth place in the Central Division with a 36-46 record, nine games behind first-place Cleveland.
In Boone's two-plus years as manager, the Royals compiled a 181-206 record.
The Royals also fired hitting coach Greg Luzinski and first base coach Mitchell Page and named former players Tom Poquette and Frank White as their replacements.
Heading into Tuesday's major league All-Star game, the Royals had lost eight games in a row and were a half-game away from tying the Minnesota Twins for last place in the division.
The 49-year-old Boone had his contract extended through 1999 after last season even though the Royals finished in last place for the first time in team history at 75-86.
Muser, 49, was Chicago's bullpen coach in 1993 and third base coach from 1994-1996 before becoming batting coach this season.

Muser spent the previous 13 years in the Milwaukee Brewers organisation, where he served as third base coach and hitting instructor. He managed Triple-A Denver from 1991-92, winning the league's Manager of the Year award when he led the team to the American Association title.
